ivory00: An ivory vertebra is a VER-teh-brul body that turns uniformly dense and white on x-ray or C-T.
ivory01: The classic differential has three causes. Metastases, lymphoma, and PAJ-it disease.
ivory02: Sclerotic metastases are the most common cause in adults. Think prostate cancer in men, and breast cancer in women. The vertebra keeps its normal size.
ivory03: Lymphoma, especially HOJ-kin lymphoma, can do the same. Look for scalloping of the front of the VER-teh-brul body from enlarged nodes beside it.
ivory04: PAJ-it disease is the one that changes shape. The vertebra is enlarged, with a thickened cortex and coarse truh-BEK-yoo-lee.
ivory05: So check the size. A normal sized ivory vertebra points to metastasis or lymphoma. An expanded one points to PAJ-it disease.
ivory06: Rarer causes include chronic infection and primary bone tumours, like OSS-tee-oh-sar-KOH-muh.
ivory07: Then look for the source. Check other bones and lymph nodes, the P-S-A in men, the breasts in women, and biopsy if needed.
ivory08: An ivory vertebra? Think metastasis, lymphoma, or PAJ-it. And always check the size.
